member_of.name: To Each His Own (initially drummer, then backup singer)

podcast.title: Dropped Out, Multiple Jobs, Independent at 17
podcast.body: Ben dropped out of school and held numerous part-time jobs, including at Second Cup, Deli's, music shops (Music World), and unloading airplanes. By age 17, he was living independently with his brothers, working three or four jobs to pay rent. "I dropped out. ... I was in the King of part-time jobs. Like I worked at second cups. I worked at Deli's. I worked at a music shop. I worked at music world. I unloaded airplanes for a long time. ... I was doing three, four jobs, you know. Because by the time I was 17, I was kind of living by myself and living with my brothers."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Billy Talent In Their Own Words: Part 1

podcast.title: Drummer Booted
podcast.body: Ben was "booted" from his drumming role in To Each His Own when Aaron Solowaniak, a more proficient drummer, was discovered practicing in a friend's basement. "And it was Aaron. And so I got the boot out of the band."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Billy Talent In Their Own Words: Part 1

podcast.title: First Singing Role
podcast.body: After being removed as the drummer, Ben was called back to To Each His Own to sing backups, a role he accepted despite never having sung before. "And I got a call about a month or two later asking if I wanted to sing backups in this band. And I was like, what? So I just wanted to be in a band. So I said, sure, I never had sung before."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Billy Talent In Their Own Words: Part 1

podcast.title: Hired at The Edge
podcast.body: Following George Stroumboulopoulos's advice, Ben emailed Phil Evans at The Edge radio station for a job interview. Despite having no high school or radio/television education, he convinced Phil Evans to hire him by promising to work harder than anyone else. "And he said, you know, when did you graduate from radio television? I'm like, I didn't. He's like, well, when did you graduate from high school? Like, I didn't. And he said, well, why should I give you the job? And I was like, because I'll work harder than anybody else. I'll come here early and I'll stay late every day. I promise. ... And as I was walking home, he called me and said, you start Monday."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Billy Talent In Their Own Words: Part 1

podcast.title: Mod Robes Job, George Stroumboulopoulos, Ted's Wrecking Yard
podcast.body: Ben worked at Mod Robes on Queen Street, selling pants. During this time, George Stroumboulopoulos would attend Pezz shows at Ted's Wrecking Yard, where Pezz became known as "the cancel band" due to frequently filling last-minute slots. "I was working at a mode robes on Queen Street selling pants. And I remember a guy named by the name of George Straumelopoulos would come and see us play because we were playing like Ted's wrecking our knowledge. We kind of became like the cancel band."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Billy Talent In Their Own Words: Part 1

podcast.title: Quit Mod Robes, Sought Radio Job
podcast.body: After watching the movie "Office Space," Ben abruptly quit his job at Mod Robes. He then contacted George Stroumboulopoulos, seeking advice on how to get a job in radio. "And I remember watching the movie Office Space and then the next day I went into mod robes and I quit. And I called George and I said, hey, I want to get a job at radio. How do I do it? How, where would I start?"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Billy Talent In Their Own Words: Part 1

podcast.title: To Each His Own Drummer
podcast.body: Ben Kowalewicz initially joined a band called To Each His Own as a drummer, having just moved to Meadowvale and meeting Trevor Bowman. "And long story short, I was the drummer in this band called To Each His Own for a minute."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Billy Talent In Their Own Words: Part 1

xref.title: Band Support for Aaron Solowoniuk and FUMS (2016)
xref.body: Billy Talent, their management, and their record label (Warner Music Canada) are 100% supportive of Aaron in his struggle with MS. They established a charity called FUMS (Fuck U MS) to raise money for MS research. At a music festival on May 29, 2016, a band member (Ben Kowalewicz) addressed the crowd, expressing the band's love, care, and commitment to Aaron, and thanking Jordan Hastings for filling in. The speaker referred to Aaron as "Mr. A. S. Lua," which appears to be a mis-transcription of his full name, Aaron Solowoniuk.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Billy Talent In Their Own Words: Part 3

xref.title: Band Rebirth - Name Change, New Songs, New Rehearsal Space
xref.body: Following a period of struggles and individual pursuits, the band experienced a "rebirth." This was catalyzed by Ian D'Sa bringing in new songs like "Try Honesty" and "Cut the Curtains," Ben Kowalewicz suggesting a band name change (from Pezz to Billy Talent), and acquiring a new rehearsal space. "And then Ben suggested we change the band name and everything just kind of came together all at once and it did feel like a rebirth and we got a new rehearsal space down the front and sure burn over here and we felt like a real band again and was up."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Billy Talent In Their Own Words: Part 1

xref.title: Departure of Future Billy Talent Members
xref.body: Ben Kowalewicz, John Gallant, and Aaron Solowaniak decided to leave To Each His Own because they wanted to pursue a heavier and different style of music than what the band was doing. "And then the three of us decided to leave that band. Which was called what? To each his own. And we decided to go, we wanted to do some heavier kind of stuff and some different kind of things."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Billy Talent In Their Own Words: Part 1

xref.title: No Lineup Changes
xref.body: Since its formation in 1993, the core lineup of Ben Kowalewicz, Ian D'Sa, John Gallant, and Aaron Solowaniak has remained constant, aside from some temporary situations. "Never. No. Never. That's insane. Yeah. There's been some temporary things here and there, but this has been the band."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Billy Talent In Their Own Words: Part 1

xref.title: Pez - Rage Against The Machine Comparison
xref.body: When Ben Kowalewicz left his radio job to pursue the band, his then-boss, Phil Evans, described the band as being "kind of like Rage Against The Machine." "Yeah, he's got this band that, you know, they're kind of like rage against the machine."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Billy Talent In Their Own Words: Part 1

xref.title: Replaced Ben as Drummer
xref.body: Aaron Solowaniak replaced Ben Kowalewicz as the drummer in the band To Each His Own, impressing the other members with his superior drumming skills. "And it was Aaron. And so I got the boot out of the band."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Billy Talent In Their Own Words: Part 1

xref.title: Talent Show Meeting - Dragonflower vs. To Each His Own
xref.body: Ian first met Ben Kowalewicz at a high school talent show where their respective bands, Dragonflower and To Each His Own, performed. He had previously met John and Aaron in classes. "The first time I met Ben was actually at a high school talent show. ... It was Dragonflower and To Each His Own plan."
